facilities.notes: The Forest Service Calhoun page lists Mac A. Callaham (Team Leader/Research Ecologist) as the only Key Personnel point of contact; a 30 Mar 2016 Calhoun CZO archive story says he became director of the experimental forest in 2016 and that Louis Metz was its first director, so Callaham is recorded as director (medium: the director title comes from a 2016 page, the current page shows him as point of contact) and Metz as former-director. Daniel Richter's Duke Scholars profile says he has directed the Long-Term Calhoun Soil-Ecosystem Experiment since 1988, recorded as lead-PI (medium: an experiment within the forest, not the forest itself). His existing founding-PI row is not supported: the Forest Service page dates the soil/vegetation archive to 1957 and the Duke page gives 1988 as when he began; left for review as not-found. The Calhoun CZO (NSF 1331846, Richter PI, co-PIs Porporato, McGlynn, Palmroth, Kumar; ended 2021) is archived and no current co-PI list was found; Markewitz's Warnell profile still lists Calhoun CZO work but no page names him co-PI. No NSF LTREB award for Calhoun was found in the NSF award API keyword results. ORCIDs: Callaham's is printed on his Forest Service profile; Richter's and Markewitz's were matched by name plus employment (Duke; UGA Warnell) on pub.orcid.org. Markewitz's Google Scholar link is on his official Warnell profile. Nicholas School profile returned 403.

The facility URL now redirects (302) to the College of Agriculture home page; the current Auburn Cullars Rotation page (cses/cullars-rotation.php) names only the managing bodies (Auburn CSES, Alabama Agricultural Experiment Station, USDA-ARS National Soil Dynamics Laboratory), no person. A Cotton Farming cover story (1 Sep 2024) states Audrey Gamble has oversight of the Old Rotation and Cullars Rotation studies and Joseph Burch performs day-to-day management; recorded as lead-PI and site-manager at medium confidence (trade-press page, titles mapped onto roles). Both appear in the current Auburn College of Agriculture directory (Gamble: Associate Professor, Soil Fertility/Soil Conservation; Burch: Research Assistant, CSES). Gamble's ORCID record shows Auburn University, Crop, Soil and Environmental Sciences, Associate Professor. A Joseph Burch ORCID lists Auburn University with no role or department; not recorded as too thin to tie. The Auburn 'Living History' article URL also redirects to the home page.

The facility URL is now 404; the current TNC preserve page (the-disney-wilderness-preserve) names no staff and says the preserve is one of four campus preserves under TNC Florida's Center for Conservation Initiatives (CCI). The CCI page is signed by Steve Coates, CCI Program Director, recorded as director of the program that runs the preserve (medium). Photo captions on the CCI page name land conservation coordinator Cody-Marie Miller at a prescribed burn on the preserve and Central Florida land conservation manager Adam Peterson monitoring the wood stork rookery on Lake Russell (which the preserve page places in the preserve); both recorded at low confidence. No named Disney Wilderness Preserve Manager was found on any TNC page; job postings for that position (2024) were seen only in search results and not used. Neither Lindsay J. Cross nor Steve Morrison appears on the preserve or CCI pages (both rows came from the 2026-05-05 recall wave).

The cooperative has no director: Maryland Sea Grant hosts its coordinator, and the Sea Grant cooperative page names Taryn Sudol as Coordinator for the Chesapeake Bay Sentinel Site Cooperative (existing row confirmed; bio added from her Maryland Sea Grant profile). Sarah Wilkins was hired in October 2015 as the first coordinator (existing past row; Sudol holds the role now). The VIMS CBSSC page that once listed an interim steering committee is now 404, NOAA's sentinel-site page redirects to a general Sea Grant topic page, and the NPS article names no people, so no steering-committee or lead is recorded. Sudol's ORCID record (0000-0002-7889-525X) shows the name but no employment; not recorded. Web search budget ran out before a further search for a current steering committee.

people.name: Mac A. Callaham
people.bio: Research ecologist and team leader with the Forest Service's Center for Forest Disturbance Science, Georgia, who also serves as the USDA Southeast Climate Hub's acting director. His work looks at how soils respond to shifting weather and environmental conditions, drawing on zoology, microbial ecology, biogeochemistry, invasion biology and restoration, especially soils under land management.
people.research_interests: Soil ecology; soil responses to weather variability; microbial ecology; biogeochemistry; invasion biology; ecosystem restoration

people.name: Daniel D. Richter
people.bio: Theodore S. Coile Distinguished Professor of Earth and Climate Sciences at Duke University's Nicholas School. Studies how human land use reshapes soils over decades to millennia, and has led the Long-Term Calhoun Soil-Ecosystem Experiment, a joint project with the USDA Forest Service in South Carolina's Piedmont, since 1988.
people.research_interests: Soil change under land use; Critical Zone science; long-term soil-ecosystem experiments; soil biogeochemistry

people.name: Daniel Markewitz
people.bio: Professor of soil-site productivity in the Warnell School, University of Georgia. Researches how nutrient and water cycling governs forest soil chemistry, drainage water and tree growth, and how soils can be managed for productivity; current projects include Calhoun CZO critical zone science, forest soil health, carbon balance of southern pine bioenergy and Amazon land-use change.
people.research_interests: Forest soil nutrient and hydrologic cycling; soil-site productivity; soil health metrics; bioenergy carbon balance in southern pines; Amazon land-use change and agroforestry

people.name: Audrey Gamble
people.bio: Associate professor of soil fertility and soil conservation in Auburn University's Department of Crop, Soil and Environmental Sciences. Research evaluates cover crops and conservation cropping systems for soil health, short-term soil health indicators as predictors of lasting gains, and nutrient recommendations for Alabama row crops.
people.research_interests: Cover crops and conservation cropping systems; soil health indicators; macro- and micronutrient fertility recommendations for row crops

people.name: Taryn Sudol
people.bio: Coordinates the Chesapeake Bay Sentinel Site Cooperative for Maryland Sea Grant, working to link research with outreach among the federal coastal reserves of the Chesapeake region and the coastal bays. She trained in conservation biology and sustainable development (MS, University of Maryland).
